transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-14
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Tom Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Marta Collins (Sundance Head of Product), Evan Li (CTO), Priya Shah (Dev Lead), Rosa Gomez (Security Lead)

[00:00] Aisha (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, really excited to kick this off. quick roll call?
[00:08] Marta (Sundance): hi all, Marta here.
[00:12] Evan (Sundance): Evan on my side.
[00:15] Priya (Sundance): Priya here.
[00:18] Rosa (Sundance): Rosa here.
[00:20] Diego (Redwood SE): Diego, SE from Redwood.
[00:22] Tom (Redwood CSM): Tom, CSM.
[00:25] Aisha: cool, agenda is quick intros, scope and success criteria, infra and security checklist, timeline and next steps, any blockers. we'll keep it tight.

[02:10] Marta: to set context - Sundance is building a patient triage assistant for our telehealth intake. we want to reduce triage time and deflect low-risk triage to a bot. key success is accuracy of routing and latency under 300ms for the happy path. cost is also a factor.

[03:05] Aisha: great, pilot scope sounds good. typical questions: are you planning to use hosted Redwood API or do you need private/VPC right away?

[03:20] Evan: security is big for us; this will touch PHI in some flows. we'd prefer private deployment or at least a VPC/private endpoint. need to understand SOC2, audit logs, encryption/KMS.

[04:02] Diego: totally understood. we offer hosted, dedicated, and private. for PHI-heavy workloads we usually recommend dedicated or private; dedicated gives reserved capacity with data isolation and private has full managed control plane in your VPC. we can walk through tradeoffs — latency, cost, and operational overhead.

[05:30] Priya: curious about integration - we mostly use AWS, EKS for services and share responses over our internal API. we'd want an SDK or simple REST calls.

[05:48] Tom: Redwood provides SDKs and a simple REST API, plus a private setup with a customer-managed VPC option. Diego can share the infra checklist and example terraform later.

[07:00] Marta: timeline wise, we want pilot in 4 weeks. is that realistic?

[07:18] Diego: 4 weeks is tight but doable for a hosted pilot. For private deployment or dedicated, provisioning may add 2-3 weeks for infra and onboarding plus security review. so hosted = fastest, dedicated = predictable throughput and quicker than full private.

[08:30] Evan: that's helpful. our SLA expectation for the pilot is mostly availability and response time, not enterprise SLA yet.

[09:05] Rosa: on security, we'll need SOC2 docs, encryption details, KMS/HSM options, SSO/SAML for users, audit logs, and data retention settings. is there a standard pack you send?

[09:25] Aisha: yes, we have a security pack. i'll share SOC2, encryption, RBAC, and audit log docs after the call. note that private deployments can integrate with customer KMS.

[10:10] Priya: on the technical side, what's the recommended model configuration? we have mixed short prompts and some long context (up to 2k tokens). cost matters.

[10:28] Diego: for triage we'd recommend a smaller instruction-tuned model — lower cost and lower latency. we can recommend quantization profiles and batching settings based on your qps. Diego: our Optimize team also has model/quantization suggestions; i can produce a cost estimate for hosted vs dedicated vs private with sample prompts.

[12:05] Marta: for KPIs, we'll track routing accuracy, reduction in triage time, and cost per session. also need guardrails for hallucination.

[12:35] Aisha: good. we'll ask you to provide sample prompts and a small eval set so Diego can run a quick sanity run during the pilot week.

[14:00] Evan: anything about data residency? we serve US and EU patients; for now pilot will be US only but longer-term we'll need EU region support.

[14:20] Diego: we support regional routing and can pin deployments to regions. for EU residency we recommend discussing private/dedicated setup or our hosted EU region.

[16:00] Rosa: about logs — how detailed are audit logs and how long do you retain them? compliance team will ask.

[16:15] Tom: audit logs include request metadata, model version, and error traces; retention depends on plan and we can arrange custom retention for enterprise. we'll include details in the security pack.

[18:00] Priya: on rollout, what's the recommended canary pattern? we want to start with 5% traffic to the model, then 25, 50.

[18:20] Diego: standard canary + A/B with rollout policies. console supports per-route rollouts, automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency spikes. we'll include a rollout runbook.

[21:30] Marta: ok let's talk about who owns what internally. i'll be product owner; Priya will do dev work and Evan is the exec sponsor. Rosa will handle security questions.

[22:15] Aisha: perfect. next immediate actions: i'll send onboarding deck + infra checklist; Diego will craft perf/cost estimate and pilot test plan; Tom will set up recurring weekly check-ins.

[24:40] Evan: one more question on failures — what's Redwood's fallback if the model is overloaded?

[25:00] Diego: we automatically route by policy; for hosted we have fallbacks to smaller models and also can send errors with graceful degradation. dedicated gives more predictable throughput.

[28:00] Rosa: any third parties or competitors we should be aware of? we evaluated Anthropic and an internal in-house prototype.

[28:20] Aisha: noted. i'll include comparative notes and the reason customers choose Redwood for production economics.

[30:00] Tom: scheduling — how about weekly 30-minute check-ins during pilot?

[30:08] Marta: works for us.

[31:00] Aisha: closing recap: share docs (onboarding deck, infra checklist, SOC2/security pack), customer to share prompts and stakeholders, SE to prepare cost/perf estimate and pilot plan, schedule weekly calls.

[32:15] Priya: will share prompts by 4/20.

[33:00] Aisha: thanks everyone. i'll follow up with calendar invites and links — look out for the onboarding deck and checklist in email.

[44:30] Meeting ended.

References and links shared: onboarding deck (link: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/deck), infra checklist (link: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/infra-checklist), SOC2/security pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-pack), pilot template (link: https://redwood.example.com/pilot/template)
